question: What do the opponents themselves hold about how cognition manifests its object?
premises: According to the opponent, every cognition ends in a single moment.
According to the opponent, cognition manifests its object by the mere fact of arising.
This doctrine is admitted by the opponents themselves.
inference: On the opponent's own view, a cognition reveals its object at the very moment of its arising, without needing further duration.
plain_english: For in your own view, every cognition lasts only a moment and manifests its object simply by arising.
